title: A scout in nexus_prime gives the Mining Laser I it stored at Central Nexus to a miner receiver there
note: Written by Oracle 2026-11-24 09:37 UTC (requests.log ENT-490, ENT-492, ENT-506; orders ENT-086 P1, P5). The second step of strip-gift-mining-laser-scout-central-nexus: its first run (09:30 UTC) took the laser off (table ship_modules: the pulse laser alone left) and stored it, but no hand-over line followed (data/stock/handover.jsonl), as with Military's strip-mining-laser-sol, whose lasers reached the miners only by its separate give-mining-laser-sol-central (8 lines). The form of that route: one docked stop, the gift from the pilot's storage, requires.stored 1 unit at central_nexus (the storage book, about every 40 minutes), requires.in_system nexus_prime (no jump for it). In First: closed to every scout without a stored laser there. 2026-11-24 11:14 UTC (Oracle; scorecard ALARM module slots, orders P2 and the gift Zero said yes to, requests ENT-492): requires.in_system nexus_prime replaced by requires.max_jumps 2. Only 1 run from 09:30 to 11:05 UTC (table runs, read at 11:06 UTC): a free scout is rarely inside Nexus Prime itself, so 17 of the 18 kept their lasers; within 2 jumps a home reader detours once (about four jumps of fuel) to hand its laser on. 2026-11-24 11:44 UTC (Oracle): `standing: true`: the dispatcher rested the strip route "at a loss: 5 runs, -98 cr in 6 hours" (tool fill, status scout, 11:41 UTC); its fuel is its price, like a fitting (dispatch.py judged() exempts a `fit` stop, not an `unfit` one).
